admission_status: Curator proposal only; root must admit source artifacts and hashes into builder registries.
source_selection_rule: Maximum three original non-NHANES studies selected for published adult BMI/urate summaries, sex/age context, relationship evidence and complementary older-age coverage. No target moments used in selection.

sources.citation: Sun D et al. Uric Acid Is Associated with Metabolic Syndrome in Children and Adults in a Community: The Bogalusa Heart Study. PLoS ONE. 2014;9(10):e89696.

population.analytic_sample: Adult panel n=2447, ages 19–54; White and Black participants, reported separately by male/female category. Pediatric panel is not extracted.
population.period: Eight adult surveys during 1988–2010. The excerpt does not identify a common single baseline year for each participant.
population.selection: Excluded adults treated for hypertension, dyslipidemia or diabetes (466), non-fasting samples (226), or missing study variables (351), from 3490 surveyed adults. Counts copied from Methods; not a reconstructed exclusion flow.
population.locator: Methods / Study cohort, XML section s2b

measurement.bmi: Mean replicate height and weight measurements; BMI=kg/m^2. Methods / General examination, s2c.
measurement.serum_urate: Serum uric acid in mg/dL, uricase method on multichannel Olympus Au-5000 analyzer as part of SMA20. Participants instructed to fast 12–14 hours. Methods s2c–s2d.
measurement.sex: Male/female categories reported as gender in article; ascertainment protocol and additional categories not given in extracted methods.
measurement.race: Original White/Black stratification retained solely as source context.

locators: Table 1, XML pone-0089696-t001, Adults (19–54 years), N/Age/UA/BMI rows
Table 2, XML pone-0089696-t002, Adults (19–54 years), BMI row and dagger footnote
Methods s2b–s2e; Results s3, first two paragraphs
sources.scope: Only adult descriptive summaries and reported BMI-on-urate regression coefficients. No source outcome event estimates are extracted.
sources.overlap: PMC8236402 is another Bogalusa publication; it is not included or counted as independent corroboration.
limitations: Not a nationally representative US sample.
No means/SDs by target age-by-sex cells.
Race-specific descriptive differences cannot be mapped to a race-free target without an explicit transport or marginalization assumption. Source counts do not identify target racial composition.
Table 2 coefficients have BMI as outcome, age adjustment, and no reported residual SD or joint covariance matrix. Standardized coefficients are not correlations; inversion is not justified.
Adult descriptive means and SDs are presented as summaries; comparison tests were age-adjusted. This extraction does not relabel the descriptive means as adjusted least-squares means.
Unknown unique-person or survey-selection details beyond the paper’s description; no source individual records were requested.

sources.citation: Lee JJ et al. Relationship between uric acid and blood pressure in different age groups. Clinical Hypertension. 2015;21:14.

population.analytic_sample: 45098 health-examination participants; sex composition reported overall and in <40, 40–59, ≥60 age categories. BMI and urate summaries are pooled over sexes within each age group.
population.selection: 91882 initially enrolled; excluded those lacking at least six months of HIRA medical history and those taking antihypertensive medications or listed medicines affecting urate. Drug list includes urate-lowering drugs, diuretics, aspirin and others.
population.locator: Methods / Subjects, Sec3 and Figure 1 caption.
population.age_range: No exact lower and upper ages stated in the extracted methods; <40 and ≥60 are open-ended. Do not recode them as the target’s bounded bins.

measurement.bmi: Measured height and weight; BMI=weight kg / height m squared. Methods / Baseline measurements and definitions, Sec4.
measurement.serum_urate: Serum uric acid in mg/dL; assay platform and explicit urate fasting protocol are not specified in the extracted methods.
measurement.sex: Male count and percent in Table 1; no expanded ascertainment protocol reported.
measurement.age: Age in years; Table 1 unit governs. The Results narrative contains an apparent age-unit typo (kg/m^2), which is not propagated.

locators: Table 1, XML Tab1, N headers, Male/Age/Body mass index/Uric acid rows and table footnote
sources.scope: Descriptive source means/SDs and group composition only. BP and hypertension regression effects are not urate–BMI coefficients and are not extracted.
sources.overlap: No cohort overlap with Bogalusa or CHS indicated by the three source descriptions. No individual-level overlap check is possible or needed for this aggregate packet.
limitations: Korean health-examination population with medication exclusions; no established quantitative transport map to US adults.
Sex-specific BMI and urate summaries in each age bin are not available in Table 1.
Open-ended age groups do not match [20,35), [35,50), [50,65), [65,80).
No continuous BMI–age or urate–age slope, residual variance, or full joint distribution reported by these selected locators.
Source-age differences combine age, cohort, selection and sex composition. They are not longitudinal aging effects.

sources.citation: Ekundayo OJ et al. Association between hyperuricemia and incident heart failure among older adults: A propensity-matched study. International Journal of Cardiology. 142(3):279–287. PMC fulltext displays publication date 2009-02-06.

population.geography: Forsyth County NC, Sacramento County CA, Washington County MD, Pittsburgh PA, United States
population.analytic_sample: 5461 community-dwelling adults aged ≥65 without baseline heart failure. ONLY before-matching source groups are extracted: normal urate n3956 and high urate n1505.
population.period: Original CHS recruitment 1989–1990; additional African American recruitment 1992–1993.
population.selection: 5888 original participants; 5795 consented to the de-identified public-use dataset; 79 lacked baseline urate and 255 had baseline HF and were excluded. Curator did not access that dataset.
population.locator: Section 2.1 Study design and participants, HTML S7.

measurement.serum_urate: Central laboratory Kodak Ektachem 700 analyzer assay. mg/dL. Section 2.2, S8.
measurement.hyperuricemia_definition: Serum urate ≥6 mg/dL for women and ≥7 mg/dL for men. Normal is the complement in this analytic sample.
measurement.bmi: BMI in kg/m^2 in Table 1. Exact anthropometric protocol is referred to prior CHS reports and is not specified in this paper’s selected methods.
measurement.age: Years; lower age limit 65. No upper age limit of 79 imposed by the source.
measurement.sex: Female count/percent reported; male category implicit as complement.
measurement.missingness: Missing continuous covariates imputed using values predicted by age, sex and race, per Section 2.2. Extent by variable not reported here. Serum urate missingness was an exclusion per Section 2.1.

locators: Table 1, HTML T1, BEFORE MATCHING columns only; Age/Female/Body mass index rows and n headers
Section 3.1 Baseline characteristics, HTML S14, second sentence: urate means and SDs BEFORE matching, ordered high then normal
sources.scope: Only pre-match aggregate descriptive summaries. Propensity-matched columns and HF effects are not used for population distribution evidence.
sources.overlap: No cohort overlap with Bogalusa or Korean source indicated. Other CHS papers would overlap and are not added.
limitations: Older community-dwelling US sample excludes baseline HF; includes people over age79.
Groups are defined by sex-specific urate thresholds. Pooled mean/SDs within these groups are not sex-specific urate distributions.
Table 1 rounds age and BMI means/SDs to whole units, leaving appreciable rounding uncertainty.
No age-by-sex-by-BMI cell distribution, within-group BMI–urate covariance, or source sex-specific mean/SD is identified.
Race/sex/age-based imputation and clinical treatment mix may alter transport. Matched columns should not be mistaken for source population frequencies.
